findings.title: Rate-limit, 5xx and network failures are still reported as an invalid token with re-auth advice.
findings.body:
Issue #14053 asks `gh auth status` to tell a 401 (token really invalid or revoked) apart from other failures (403 rate limit, 5xx, TLS/DNS). For those other failures it should stop saying "The token in X is invalid." and stop suggesting `gh auth refresh`, which the issue says makes a rate-limited account look worse.

This change only adds an `- Error: ...` line, and only when stderr is a TTY. With a 403 rate limit or a 503, the output still says the token is invalid and still tells the user to re-authenticate. The new tests lock this in: the 503 case in hunk 6 and the rate-limit, server-error and network-error cases in hunk 11 still expect the invalid-token wording.

The issue's own trigger is an agent or CI loop, which usually runs with stderr not on a TTY. In that case the output doesn't change at all.

Fix: classify on the HTTP status (401 means invalid; anything else means "Could not verify token: <error>" with no refresh hint), as the issue asks. Also show the error even when stderr is not a TTY.
